p.i: tum charum habeas animo, nec defrau-des eum libertate. Pecudes si tibi fuerint, fac cures eas: & si tibi sunt utiles, apud te permaneant. Si liberi tibi fuerint, e-rudias eos, & ceruicem eorum domes à iuuentute. Si filiae tibi sint, asserues corpus earum, nec vultum tuum offendas i-is hilarem. Eloca filiam, & magnum opus peregeris. Caterum fac eam viro cor-dato colloces. Vxorem ex sententia na-tus ne repudies, nec te permittas odiosa.

main_text.p: I Discimus ex verbis illis, qualem uxorem sibi quisque eligere & accipere, & vero etiam retinere debeat, nempe sapientem & bonam. Inquit enim, μὴ ἀπόχι[?]ς γαυκὸς σοφῆς & ἀγαθῆς. So wirstu es wol treffen/und nit fallen. dicerisque [illegible, ~5 letters]. Sapiens est, quae timet Dominum (unde Latinus interpres addit, quam fortitus es in timore Domini .i. quam Domini metuentem natus es) & sapientiam .i. Christum, eiusque spiritum in se habet manentem per fidem. Haec vero sapientia inuenitur in Scripturis sanctis, ac discitur ex Dei verbo, & comparatur precibus fidei à Deo, 2. Tim. 3. Psalm. 119. Iacob 1. Bona vel proba mulier est, quae à Deo bona reddita, ex bono thesauro cordis sui depromit bona, virtuosa, honesta, ἀγαθὴ καὶ ἀλ[?]α- ἀγαθοποιοῦσα, edens fructum spiritus, ἀγαθωσύνην,

page.notes: The Greek in the second paragraph is only partly legible: the opening word after μὴ, the word before ἀγαθοποιοῦσα and the word after dicerisque are doubtful or illegible. The black-letter line is a German quotation set in bold black letter. The horizontal marks beneath the last line are show-through or stray marks and were not transcribed. The first paragraph is italic and continues from the previous page, so it is marked cont="true". The printed "I" before "Discimus" is a section numeral and is kept in the paragraph.
